label: Local Eatery
register: The buyer is evaluating whether this feels like a beloved, authentic neighborhood institution worth traveling for, judged against other legendary local food spots rather than generic restaurant chains.

sites.name: Franklin Barbecue
sites.why: Leads with a third-party editorial quote (Texas Monthly) instead of self-praise, instantly signaling 'worth the line' credibility.

sites.name: Pat's King of Steaks
sites.why: Hero anchors on a giant 'SINCE 1930' heritage stamp plus pop-culture press logos (Food Network, Rocky), turning nostalgia into trust signals above the fold.

sites.name: Pike Place Chowder
sites.why: Stacks concrete, numbered proof ('17 First-Place awards,' James Beard, MSC certification) right under the hero claim instead of vague superlatives.

sites.name: Russ & Daughters
sites.why: A single 'since 1914' line does the trust-building work, paired with a minimal, generously-spaced layout that reads as heirloom rather than corporate.

sites.name: Voodoo Doughnut
sites.why: Seasonal hero imagery refreshed with limited-time products keeps the homepage feeling alive and worth revisiting, not a static brochure page.

sites.name: Katz's Delicatessen
sites.why: Site name itself ('NYC's oldest deli') functions as a persistent trust badge baked into the browser tab and header, reinforcing institution status site-wide.
